correctness.rationale: For all finite {1,2} suffixes, prove that the cost-to-go F is nondecreasing by discrepancy parity and F(2)-F(0) lies in [0,2]. Backward induction then forces the lower-imbalance successor to be globally optimal. Four-good exact opposing assignments prove sharp failure at 3 and at 0; the reverse triangle inequality proves no length-under-four nonnegative counterexample exists. Check.py independently compares direct enumeration, dynamic programming, and the claimed greedy rule on explicitly bounded test domains; finite tests are not invoked as an infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: This theorem is about absolute load discrepancy for each fixed exogenous arrival sequence, equivalently cumulative maximum directed envy for two agents with identical valuations. It is not equivalent to zero-one prefix balancing: a positive size-two good may force a temporary discrepancy of 2, and a zero-valued good can preserve earlier regret. Nor is a guarantee from sorting the goods equivalent to the fixed-order claim; sorting changes the admissible solutions.

value.rationale: Cumulative envy is the principal numerical objective of the initiating work, where unrestricted two-agent identical values are hard and {0,1} is the tractable benchmark. Allowing values {1,2} introduces nontrivial temporary imbalance and no pointwise-best prefix rule, yet the simple online rule remains optimal against full foresight for all arrival orders. The exact {1,2}-versus-3 and positivity-versus-zero boundaries clarify the first structural enlargement and failure of a natural fairness algorithm; not merely a bounded enumeration.
